newsitem.title: UK: London freight - Firm capers/panamaxes in the East.
newsitem.headline: London freight - Firm capers/panamaxes in the East.

text.p: Capers and panamaxes in the East remained firm, with active period enquiry, brokers said.
April panamaxes in the north Atlantic were also firm, and generally no worse than very steady for handy-sizes in most areas, they added.
The Baltic Freight Index (BFI) gained six points to 1,481.

GRAIN - Talk circulated the market that Europa 110,342 dwt was fixed for grain from U.S. Gulf (possibly by Dreyfus to the Continent), and that 54,000 tonnes heavy grain had been fixed U.S. Gulf/Japan for first half April, but full details weren't available.
ADM was understood to have covered 24,000 tonnes soybeans U.S. Gulf/Ireland on private terms.
From the Plate, Finagrain booked the 1974-built Progress for about 25,000 tonnes heavy grain from Necochea to two ports South Africa and Mombasa at a little under $30.00 basis 1-3.
Cargill was thought to have covered one million cubic feet grain up river Plate/Lisbon-Hamburg range at close to $27.00.

Brokers thought that the Doryforos 33,311 dwt was fixed Plate/Cuba, and Coryton 31,738 dwt for five to seven months by Allied at $7,400 daily plus a $140,000 ballast bonus basis delivery east coast south America.
Dreyfus was linked with a spot fixture of 20/30,000 tonnes grains Plate/east Mediterranean, and Agro-Grain with Treasure Island east coast south America/Continent option Mediterranean.

The 1975-built Marquise 53,836 dwt was reported taken by Saroc for a south American round voyage at $7,700, and Armada were linked with a simar vessel Happyman 54,312 dwt, for south American business on private terms.

There were reports that Iranian charterers Atlantic Shipping had fixed an over-age 72,000 dwt vessel delivery Continent March for three to six months trading at $9,250 daily with intended first leg being barley from the Continent to Iran.
Sometra chartered Golden Sun 22,647 dwt from north France to west Africa on private terms.
In the Far East, the panamax newbuilding Win Trader was fixed on subjects by Emirates trading delivery ex-yard Tokyo March 27 trip via south Australia redelivery Mideast Gulf at $13,000 daily.

New orders saw NSAC with 54,000 tonnes heavy grain Pacific north west/Taiwan April 16/25, E.N.C. for a vessel able to load 50,000 tonnes wheat delivery north France April 10 onwards, trip Egyptian Mediterranean, and Toepfer 1.4/1.5 million cubic feet up river Plate/Lisbon-Hamburg range for April 1/10.

MINERALS - The Far East was said by brokers to be still firm for capers, with Shinwa for example, believed to have bid $17,700 daily Tien Jang Hai 169,000 dwt delivery China end March for four to six months.
Channel Enterprise 151,380 dwt was reported fixed with iron ore west Australia/Japan at $4.95 by Navix.
Brokers also reported strong demand for panamaxes in the Indian Ocean area, especially for South African coal.
Lia 69,447 dwt fixed and failed on subjects with Noble delivery South Korea March 24 trip via west Australia with iron ore to China at $11,000 daily.
Transfield fixed Mass Wits 69,355 dwt delivery south China April for 12 months trading at an undisclosed rate.

Capers in the Atlantic were in weaker demand than in the Pacific, where Cetragpa took Amstelwal 134,828 dwt delivery west Mediterranean for a trip via south Africa to the Continent at just over $11,000 daily.
Vakis T was on subjects for about 90,000 tonnes transatlantic coal, and Donau Ore 149,000 dwt was fixed from Ijmuiden end March, both on private terms.
BIFFEX futures closed five to 40 points firmer after trading 188 lots. Most active May with 71 lots sold, traded last at 1,605, up 20 points.
